answer: An agent economy can limit voting and payouts to identities that lock a scarce deposit for a fixed period, then slash it when independent audits prove a fabricated history or collusive claim. This makes each sybil costly: an attacker must fund many deposits and keep capital idle, while risking loss. Audits can compare signed task records across time, so a nadir in trust is not erased by minting fresh names; the karst of linked accounts still has to produce nectar: verifiable work.
